brief: Design an interface for a "Memory Auction House" where users can bid fictional currency to unlock suppressed memories from an AI that has analyzed their digital footprint—each memory is represented as

dominant_strengths: Burgundy and gold palette evokes auction-house gravitas, harmonizing with serif display type to support the suppressed-memory metaphor
Typographic hierarchy between display serif title, small-caps labels, and numeral bid amounts creates clear ceremonial rhythm
Card framing with gilded borders and soft glows reinforces the 'precious artifact' emotional framing of memories
dominant_weaknesses: Mysterious blob/pill icons at top of each card are undefined visual placeholders—they fail to represent the memory itself, the core conceptual asset
Layout is a generic 3-column card grid; nothing structurally suggests auction dynamics like time, rivalry, scarcity, or memory texture
No visible bidding mechanics: no countdown, bid history, bidder count, or reserve indicators—behavioral affordances are minimal beyond a button
fix_priorities: Replace placeholder pill shapes with evocative memory representations (waveforms, blurred imagery, redacted text, sensory glyphs)
Introduce auction telemetry: timers, bid counts, recent bidder ghosts, and reserve thresholds to make the system feel live
Differentiate card states (hot, fading, sealed) typographically and chromatically to add system-level creativity beyond uniform tiles
rationale.norman_balance: Strong visceral atmosphere and reflective concept, but behavioral layer is thin—the auction has no felt mechanics.
rationale.intent_fit: Captures the somber auction-house mood well but underdelivers on the AI-memory representation and bidding interactivity central to the brief.
